## Full trie sync now stamps graph freshness: every sync path that begins with a… — 2026-07-30 (parent 06247def315f)

**Full trie syncs now stamp graph freshness so the next turn-hook graph-only sync no-ops, plus agent-facing tool descriptions for grep, commit, and patch_apply are updated to match actual return envelopes.**

Four sync entry points — `_run_full_pass`, `_run_incremental_sync`, `_run_metadata_only_refresh`, and `_run_roles_only_sync` — now call the new `stamp_graph_fresh` helper after completing their whole-project scan. This writes the current HEAD + in-scope mtimes stamp, so the follow-up graph-only sync (turn hook) detects a fresh graph and exits without rebuilding. Single-file sync is deliberately excluded: a partial scan would mask other files' edits.

`stamp_graph_fresh` is an advisory no-op outside git or before the first commit.

Regression coverage is added in `test_full_sync_stamps_graph_freshness`, which asserts that both bootstrap and incremental paths write the stamp and that the immediate graph-only follow-up reports "graph fresh".

On the documentation side:
- `TrieTools.grep` docstring and the generated opencode tool description now document the `related`/`related_kind` fill-up keys and that fallback matches are capped by the caller's limit.
- `TrieTools.commit` docstring documents the `uncovered` key returned at apply time.
- `_render_opencode_patch_apply` tells agents to expect gate-coverage output so they can re-stage immediately.
